claim_ceiling: A property of a constructed object. It is a SELECTION SET and nothing measured on it is a conclusion about real items.

reported_only_no_criterion_adjusted.why_it_is_recorded: requirement 2 is a statement about vocabularies; this is a statement about behaviour. If the model were emitting the letter, the requirement would hold on paper while the object behaved differently in practice

requirement_3_anti_retrieval.comparison: drop >= required_drop; the floor is the value P-0c measured, so this object must be at least as anti-retrievable as its predecessor
requirement_3_anti_retrieval.probe: the same prompt with the queried name's own registration line removed
requirement_3_anti_retrieval.why_it_is_the_right_probe: it removes the FIRST hop's input while leaving the second hop's clue, the rules table, entirely intact

verbatim: The model answers the rebuilt two-hop items at or above the registered accuracy floor of 0.80, and removing the first hop's input collapses accuracy to chance with a drop at least as large as the one its predecessor achieved. The intermediate is therefore known BY CONSTRUCTION and required BY THE TASK, and the object may serve as the selection set on which candidate estimands are compared. THIS IS A PROPERTY OF A CONSTRUCTED OBJECT AND NOTHING ELSE. It is not a result about real items, it is not a phenomenon-level positive control for any borrowed item set, and it licenses no claim about J-space, the J-lens, the paper, or T. A constructed object is a SELECTION SET, and success on a selection set is not success on an application set.
